observations: A broad rectangular form sits centered on a teal ground, outlined in thick black; its upper edge sprouts a row of sharp white spikes and a band of yellow-green hatching.
Two recessed rectangular zones suggest eye sockets: the left holds crossed yellow-orange loops, the right a dark oval ringed by red and orange ellipses on a white field.
A wide horizontal rectangle near the bottom, bordered in deep red, contains dense black scribble lines on white, sitting as a filled band rather than open space.
reading: The face reads as architecture more than anatomy—stacked rectangular chambers, each holding its own color argument. The spiked crown presses upward while the scribble-filled lower band anchors the structure downward. Thin magenta and yellow lines drift outside the thick black borders, loosening what those outlines try to contain. The mood sits between ceremonial weight and barely controlled noise.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #77 and #79. Where #77 fills a red ground with a rounded organic mass and #79 opens onto flat sky-blue with a single spiral eye, #78 builds a cooler teal field around a rigid, compartmented structure.

connections.reason: Both works use stacked rectangular eye zones and a wide mouth band, but #77 rounds its outer silhouette against red while #78 keeps hard right-angle edges against teal, sharpening the structural contrast.
nnotb #256 shares the spiked crown and layered rectangular face chambers visible in #78, though it builds on black rather than teal and extends the composition below the face into a torso region.

lookingQuestion: How does the behavior of the thin colored lines outside the thick black border change your sense of where the face ends and the background begins?
ambiguities: The right eye zone contains a dark oval and red-orange ellipses; whether this reads as a single eye or two overlapping forms is not fully resolved by the image alone.
Title-derived and recorded-creation neighbor orders align for this work, but gaps may exist elsewhere in the owned subset, so sequence position should not be read as strict making order.
